home.name: Logan Thompson
home.news: The Capitals' starting goalie will not be confirmed until warmups at 7:00 PM ET. Thompson has quietly become one of the NHL's most consistent and reliable goalies over the past several seasons, coming off consecutive 31-win campaigns. Despite some struggles at the start of the 2026-27 season, allowing three or more goals in three of his last four (1-3-0) and posting a 3.58 GAA and .880 SV%, the Capitals are eagerly awaiting Thompson's return, as he has missed the past two games.

away.name: Devin Cooley
away.news: Cooley has been phenomenal lately, making Head Coach Ryan Huska's decision to turn to him for a fifth consecutive game easy. The 29-year-old California-born goalie saved 26 of 28 shots (.929 SV%) in his most recent outing, a 5-2 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs. He has an outstanding 1.50 GAA and .955 SV% in his last four games (4-0-0). The Flames enter Wednesday's contest as +162 road underdogs against an Edmonton Oilers team that has scored three or more goals in 11 of 12 games this season (8-2-2).

away.name: Jake Allen
away.news: With the recent acquisition of three-time Vezina winner Connor Hellebuyck, Allen will likely see a lighter workload for the Devils, but he will tend the twine on Wednesday in the tail end of a back-to-back. The 36-year-old Allen has been serviceable, albeit unspectacular this season, posting a 2.84 GAA and .886 SV% in seven games (5-2-0). He had a light workload in his most recent outing, saving 12 of 13 shots (.923 SV%) in a 3-1 win over the Los Angeles Kings. The Devils enter Wednesday's matchup as +124 road underdogs against a Colorado Avalanche team that has lost three of its last four games (1-3-0).

home.name: Mackenzie Blackwood
home.news: The Avalanche have been treading water in recent games, losing six of their last 10 (4-5-1), with suspect goaltending at least partly to blame. That said, Blackwood has been far more reliable than Wedgewood recently and is coming off a 31-save performance (.912 SV%) in a 6-3 win over the Tampa Bay Lightning. The 29-year-old Blackwood has 2.53 GAA and .914 SV% in his last four games (3-1-0). Colorado enters Wednesday's contest as -136 home favourites against a red-hot New Jersey Devils team that has outscored opponents 16-6 in their last four games (4-0-0).
